question: When do those Signals run, and can they stop a bad answer before the user sees it?

observer.firstAnswerText:
Signals aren't meant to stop answers. They're described as monitoring that scores agent turns and shows the results in the Agents view [S1, S17]. Signals that use your own HTTP endpoint (a remote scorer) are documented to run after a turn finishes and in the background [S14, S15], so they can't block a reply. For the default LLM-judge signals, the docs I read don't say exactly when scoring happens. Nothing I read says they can block a response either.

When Signals run

Remote-scorer signals: A turn counts as finished when its root span ends. A span is a record of one operation, and the root span is the top-level one for the turn. Weave then sends out a weave.genai.turn_ended event. A scoring worker checks the project's active signals, applies each one's filters and sample rate, calls your endpoint, and saves the result as feedback on the turn. The result then shows on the Signals tab [S14].
This scoring is asynchronous, meaning it doesn't happen as part of your agent's response. If a result is missing, check that the turn matched the filters and sample rate and that its root span ended [S15]. Failed attempts can be retried for up to 30 seconds, and Weave records nothing if every attempt fails [S14, S15].
LLM-judge signals: An LLM judge scores each agent turn. You can limit which turns are scored with filters and a sample rate. After you create the signal, Weave scores matching turns [S16]. I'm inferring that these also run after the turn, like remote-scorer signals, but the pages I read don't say so directly.

If you need to block responses

That's what Weave guardrails do. They score the user's input or the model's output in real time, before it reaches the user, and can block or change a response when a score crosses a threshold [S6].
Guardrails need code changes because they change what your app does next. They work through scorers you call directly in your Python code. The TypeScript SDK doesn't support setting them up [S9].
I only read the guardrails overview sections, and they don't cover using guardrails with the Agents/Signals setup. In practice, you'd add the blocking check in your agent's code and keep using Signals to monitor afterward.
